facts.text: Lenni-Lenape Native Americans originally inhabited the fertile valleys and streams around Pennside for hunting and agriculture prior to European arrival.
English Quakers, including the Boone family, began settling the Exeter Township portion of Pennside in the early eighteenth century.
Early economic life in Pennside centered on agriculture and milling, including a sawmill that produced gunpowder during the Revolutionary War.
The Philadelphia-Reading Railroad line and early stagecoach routes helped connect Pennside to Reading and beyond by the mid-nineteenth century.
Pennside is situated on the hills of Mount Penn, approximately three miles northwest of downtown Reading.
The local landscape of Pennside features a mix of forested areas and developed surfaces, reflecting a suburban-rural interface.
